summary: recce/ad/kerberos.py is a hand-rolled ASN.1 DER Kerberos client (TCP/88 only) that covers the pre-auth-less trio — AS-REP roasting, username enumeration, and PA-ETYPE-INFO2 preflight — plus RC4-HMAC credentialed Kerberoasting (with AES 17/18 accepted from the KDC but not encryptable client-side). Missing: every attack primitive that requires AES-CTS-HMAC-SHA1 crypto, PKINIT, or S4U/U2U message building; pre-auth password spraying; PAC parsing; and every 2020-2022 name-service CVE (noPac, Bronze Bit, RC4 downgrade). It also does not feed confirmed usernames, salts, cracked hashes, or realm-confirmations back into recce's cross-service stores.

missing_capabilities.name: Kerberos pre-auth password spraying (AS-REQ + PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP)
missing_capabilities.description: The module has all the primitives (rc4_encrypt + _build_as_req_preauth) to send a real pre-authenticated AS-REQ but never uses them for spraying a candidate password against the enumerated user list. KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED (24) vs a returned AS-REP is a clean success/fail oracle that raises event 4771 (usually unmonitored), NOT 4625 (SMB spray), and does not increment the SMB lockout counter on most policies — the quietest domain spray primitive available. This is the natural chain after user_enum: recce confirms 50 usernames, then it should spray 'Winter2026!' against them right there.

missing_capabilities.name: AES-CTS-HMAC-SHA1 client-side crypto (etypes 17/18)
missing_capabilities.description: Module states explicitly 'RC4-only (etype 23) — stdlib-friendly (no AES in the standard library).' Consequence: any AS-REQ with pre-auth against an account where msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes disables RC4 (Windows Server 2022+ default; explicitly hardened tenants) cannot be crafted, so credentialed kerberoast, spraying, and S4U all fail against modern AD. AES128/256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 with PBKDF2 (RFC 3962) is implementable in stdlib (hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac + a CTS mode helper). Without it recce is a legacy-RC4 tool.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 3961 §6.3, RFC 3962 §4 (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96, iter count 4096, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 string-to-key)

missing_capabilities.name: noPac / sAMAccountName spoofing (CVE-2021-42278 + CVE-2021-42287)
missing_capabilities.description: Rename a computer account (or created machine via MachineAccountQuota) to 'DC01' with no trailing $, request a TGT for it, then rename it back and use S4U2Self to obtain a TGT for a Domain Admin against the real DC01$ (KDC falls back on prefix lookup). recce has AS-REQ, KRB-ERROR classification, and TGS-REQ primitives; adding the rename-race + S4U2Self step turns Kerberos foothold into instant domain compromise on any DC missing the Nov-2021 KB. No detection of unpatched KDCs today.

missing_capabilities.name: S4U2Self / S4U2Proxy (MS-SFU) — constrained delegation & Bronze Bit
missing_capabilities.description: No PA-FOR-USER (S4U2Self) or additional-tickets (S4U2Proxy) message construction. With a service-account credential recce cannot impersonate a Domain Admin against that service's SPN (the standard delegation abuse chain: printerbug/webclient coerce -> RBCD write -> S4U). Also blocks Bronze Bit (CVE-2020-17049): flip forwardable bit on the returned ticket, S4U2Proxy against a target that would otherwise refuse — protection-level test AND primitive. Both are the top-tier AD escalation attacks currently unrepresented.

missing_capabilities.name: PKINIT (RFC 4556) + UnPAC-the-hash
missing_capabilities.description: No PA-PK-AS-REQ construction. Shadow-Credentials attack (msDS-KeyCredentialLink write from a lesser-priv, then PKINIT-auth as the target) currently has no auth path inside recce — the LDAP side of the write is doable elsewhere but recce cannot then obtain the TGT. UnPAC-the-hash (PKINIT -> U2U TGS -> PAC_CREDENTIAL_INFO decrypts to the target's NT hash) is likewise unreachable. This is the standard modern (post-'ain't-my-fault-msDS-KeyCredentialLink-is-writable') AD path from cert to NT hash.

missing_capabilities.name: PAC parsing on AS-REP / TGS-REP
missing_capabilities.description: asrep_hash captures cipher bytes for cracking but no code decrypts (RC4-side we CAN, we have the key from PA-ENC-TS spray) or parses the PAC. Parsing PAC_LOGON_INFO gives primary group RID, SID history, group SID array, logon domain — a free BloodHound-lite group dump per successful auth. PAC_CREDENTIAL_INFO (PKINIT branch) gives the NT hash. Currently zero PAC awareness even though recce holds the session key on the credentialed path.

missing_capabilities.name: RC4-HMAC etype downgrade detection & policy check
missing_capabilities.description: PA-ETYPE-INFO2 preflight reports has_rc4/aes_only per user but there is no domain-wide roll-up: how many accounts still allow RC4? A domain that ships krbtgt with RC4 enabled (default until Nov-2022 hardening / CVE-2022-37966) means every TGT can be forged with an NT hash instead of AES key — the classic Golden Ticket precondition. Also: no detection of DES (etype 1/3) still being accepted, which is a hard fail against modern CIS baselines.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 4120 §7.5.1 etype table; MSRC CVE-2022-37966 (RC4 removal); CIS AD Domain L1 2.3.11.1

missing_capabilities.name: AS-REP roasting for machine accounts and DONT_REQ_PREAUTH on krbtgt/trust accounts
missing_capabilities.description: candidate_users explicitly filters '$' names ('# skip machine accounts'). Computer accounts with pre-auth disabled DO exist (rare but real, and trust-account $ names — DOMAIN$ trust-in — are AS-REP roastable and yield the trust key -> full inter-realm ticket forging). Also no explicit probe for krbtgt/OLD or krbtgt with DONT_REQ_PREAUTH set (a badly staged password reset can leave it that way). One-line fix but zero coverage.

missing_capabilities.name: KDC time-skew disclosure + fingerprinting
missing_capabilities.description: KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW (37) responses include the KDC's ctime/cusec — an unauthenticated server-clock oracle useful for cache-timing / replay windows and for detecting a KDC drifting off NTP (attacker-controlled DHCP+NTP scenarios). Also nothing distinguishes MIT/Heimdal/AD KDCs — behavioral fingerprinting via error codes (AD emits STATUS_ codes in e-data, Heimdal does not) drives which follow-on attacks apply.

missing_capabilities.name: Kerberos over UDP + fragmentation (RFC 4120 §7.2.1)
missing_capabilities.description: _send_recv is TCP-only. UDP/88 is the default for many MIT/Heimdal deployments and some AD sites; a firewall that permits UDP/88 but drops TCP/88 currently reads as 'no KDC'. UDP is also the classic path for the KRB-ERROR truncation fingerprint (an AS-REP over the MTU forces KRB_ERR_RESPONSE_TOO_BIG=52) — a reliable AD-vs-MIT signal.

missing_capabilities.name: kpasswd probe (TCP/UDP 464)
missing_capabilities.description: The Kerberos password-change protocol on port 464 is often exposed alongside 88 and supports a set-password variant that requires only a valid TGT and the target principal (no old password) — the exact primitive Impacket's changepasswd.py uses after AS-REP-roasting or noPac. recce does not scan for or interact with 464 today, so a critical post-crack pivot is invisible.

missing_capabilities.name: FAST / armoring detection (RFC 6113)
missing_capabilities.description: FAST-armored AS-REQ hides PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP inside a FAST tunnel, defeating pre-auth password spraying and preventing PA-ETYPE-INFO2 leakage. Detecting whether the KDC advertises PA-FX-FAST (PA-DATA type 136) tells the operator whether spraying is even viable and, conversely, whether AS-REP roasting is still the ONLY path. Zero awareness currently.

cross_service_wire_gaps: Confirmed valid usernames (state='valid') from roast_user do not feed a cross-service known_users store — LDAP anonymous, SMB spray, HTTP form login all re-derive names instead of consuming this authoritative list.

AS-REP hashes ($krb5asrep$23$…) and TGS hashes ($krb5tgs$…) captured in results/findings are not registered into a hashes/credentials store — the crack pipeline is on the operator, not orchestrated, and a later cracked password does not automatically re-fan out into SMB/LDAP/MSSQL spray.

Salt strings from parse_etype_info2 leak the canonical sAMAccountName case AND the realm (salt = REALMsAMAccountName for user accounts, host/fqdn@REALM for computer accounts) — free feed for known_hostnames and known_domains but not published.
The KDC's confirmed realm from a KRB-ERROR reply (crealm field) is authoritative and could seed known_domains with source='kerberos', but analyze() only consumes known_domains, never writes back.

SPNs used successfully in kerberoast_spn (host/fqdn:port, MSSQLSvc/fqdn:1433, HTTP/fqdn, CIFS/fqdn) name real listening services — should register the fqdn side into known_hostnames and the port hint into a services-to-probe queue (mssql/http/smb).

Detected pre-auth-disabled accounts are prime relay victims when they are computer accounts — should be flagged in relay_targets with the extra signal 'DONT_REQ_PREAUTH', which strengthens NTLM/Kerberos relay outcomes.

KDC identity (the DC's IP/fqdn) confirmed by an AS-REP is the authoritative DC pointer — currently used only locally in the module, not published as 'domain_controller' role into hosts metadata for LDAPS/SMB modules to prioritise.
priority_gaps: Kerberos pre-auth password spray (AS-REQ + PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP against enumerated users) — highest-ROI: primitives already exist in the module, one loop + KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED (24) classification, quiet vs SMB spray, chains directly off the existing user_enum finding.

AES-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 client-side crypto (RFC 3962 PBKDF2 + CTS mode) — unblocks kerberoast/spray/S4U against RC4-disabled AD tenants which is now the default; without it recce silently degrades against modern domains.

noPac (CVE-2021-42278/42287) + S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy PA-FOR-USER message construction — the two dominant credential-to-DA escalation paths in AD pentests; both are pure DER + KDC exchange work atop what recce already builds.

PAC parsing on the credentialed path — recce already holds the session key on kerberoast_spn; decrypting the PAC yields group SIDs, admin membership, and (via PKINIT/U2U) the NT hash. Free intelligence per successful roast, and prerequisite for UnPAC-the-hash.
notes: Module is well-scoped for the credential-less trio but architecturally pinned to RC4 ('no AES in the standard library'); the single most impactful investment is a stdlib AES-CTS implementation because it unblocks half of the other listed gaps (spray, S4U, PKINIT UnPAC on modern KDCs). Cross-service publishing is the second-biggest hole: everything the module learns (realm, users, salts, hashes, SPN-derived hostnames, DC role) stays local and forces every other module to rediscover it.
